newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan opposition party denounces isles protest.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan opposition party denounces isles protest.

text.p: Taiwan's main opposition party on Tuesday denounced the landing by Taiwan and Hong Kong activists on Japan-held islands as "barbaric", saying the joint mission compromised Taiwan's claim of sovereignty over the isles.

The Democratic Progressive Party, proclaiming that Taiwan alone owned the deserted East China Sea islands, released a poll showing most Taiwan people disagreed with the protest voyage. The activists had sought to assert Chinese sovereignty over the rocky outcrops in the East China Sea.

Taiwan is ruled by a government that lost the civil war to the Chinese communists in 1949 and went into exile on the island. Recent years have seen a growing movement, spearheaded by the opposition party, to abandon Taiwan's goal of reunification with the mainland and to pursue independence.
On Monday Taiwan independence activists had demonstrated against the raising of the flags of the rival Chinas on the disputed islands on Monday.

"The Diaoyu islands belong to Taiwan, and Taiwan does not belong to China," the Democratic Progressive Party said in a statement. "The barbaric behaviour (of the mission members) not only shows severe ignorance of international political reality, but also is contradictory."

Recent protests against Tokyo's claim to the islands -- called the Diaoyus in Chinese and the Senkakus in Japanese -- have united Chinese nationalist groups in Taiwan, Hong Kong and China. Hong Kong, at present a British territory, reverts to Chinese sovereignty in mid-1997.
Chinese nationalism led to Monday's joint Taiwan-Hong Kong mission, which the opposition poll said was hailed by some Taiwanese as an heroic accomplishment but was denounced by most.

The survey, which did not say how many were polled and gave no margin of error, said 52.6 percent of Taiwan people disagreed with the mission and up to 62.3 percent believed Taiwan alone held sway over the islands.
Only 10.2 percent said the they were owned jointly by Taiwan and China, while 33.3 percent said they supported the protest voyage.

Supporters of Taiwan independence hurled eggs, burned communist China's flag and shouted slogans such as "beat communist bandits" at a rally on Tuesday outside a Taipei hotel where Hong Kong members of the protest flotilla were staying.
